entries.text: Milstein’s stereo remake of the complete sonatas and partitas is late modern-instrument Bach: polished, dance-aware, closer to the manuscript than his earlier Capitol mono cycle. Against Podger’s baroque-violin set it is the other side of the argument — the great modern statement rather than gut and implied polyphony. Not the Référence on this shelf — that goes to the HIP first choice.

entries.text: Podger’s complete gut-strung cycle hears Bach’s counterpoint and implied polyphony on a baroque violin. Against Milstein’s DG remake it is the other stance: HIP clarity while modern staples still owned the shop. The Chaconne accumulates; ornamentation stays alive without fuss. Référence for the complete solo cycle on period violin.
